Starting at a target singleton, productive steps leave circular intervals starting at 0. To expand again the interval must start at 1, requiring n-1 inverse rotations. The n-1 growths and n-2 minimal internal runs force W_n at equality. One extra letter is at a rotation boundary or gives an insertion of b into W_n. In the j-th split, the reverse interval at the insertion has length n-j and first point t+1 modulo n. Its endpoint is 0 precisely at t=j; shrinking makes coverage impossible with n total b's. Other interior offsets fix the interval; t=0 doubles b harmlessly, while t=n-1 represents the next doubling or W_nb. This verifies the single-factor family rather than relying on finite testing. On C_3 the post-initial set is {1,2}; a^2 b collapses, while a^0 b and a^1 b fix the set. In a nondivisible split, t=2 mod 3 collapses immediately, t=0 does not, and t=1 collapses exactly when the remaining exponent is 2 mod 3 (n=1 mod 3). Boundary extensions cannot help. At n=3 both factors share unique W_3=baab; n=4,5 and all later nondivisible cases have the eligible (n-2,n-3) split. Of the (3k-1)*2k or 3k*k pairs exactly 2k or k violate t!=j, giving the stated counts.
